traits.bark_colour.note: The bark colour chosen by eye for appearance (see its note), as a screen colour: it stood as appearance.bark [0.42, 0.38, 0.34], which is linear light, so the trunk drew pale grey to white beside photographs of the species (2026-10-23). It stands here in sRGB, as bark colours are picked, and the bark rule (tracheophyta) turns it into linear light.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_max_m.note: FEIS's Alaska-cedar review (Griffith 1992, read 2026-10-15): "It can obtain heights of 100 to 125 feet (30-38 m)".

traits.leaf_length_m.note: FEIS's Alaska-cedar review (Griffith 1992, read 2026-10-15): "The leaves are scalelike and roughly 0.125 inch (0.32 cm) in length".

traits.cone_length_m.note: FEIS's Alaska-cedar review (Griffith 1992, read 2026-10-15): "The female strobili are green, spherical, and 0.5 inch (1 cm) in diameter".

traits.sexual_system.note: FEIS's Alaska-cedar review (Griffith 1992, read 2026-10-15): "a native, evergreen, long-lived ... monoecious tree".

generator.params.note: Western redcedar's values, changed by hand for Alaska cedar: a narrow crown (FEIS, Griffith 1992: "slow growing with a narrow crown") and the strongly drooping, hanging branchlet sprays of the species. height_rate set so it reaches its reference height in a stand, where its drooping leader and dense sprays slow it. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 15 m tall and 45 cm across at 60 years in a stand, set by hand a little under western redcedar's 27 m (FEIS calls Alaska cedar slow-growing, Griffith 1992) with the girth the conifer program gives that height. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: By eye: grey, shreddy bark (FEIS: "the bark is shreddy"); dull blue-green hanging sprays; round green cones.
